ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in a $4\times4$ square grid, each small square has a side length of $1$. Points $A$, $B$, and $C$ are all on the grid points, and $AD\perp BC$ at point $D$. What is the length of $AD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} From the Pythagorean theorem, we have: $AB =\sqrt{2^{2}+4^{2}}=2\sqrt{5}$, $AC =\sqrt{1^{2}+2^{2}}=\sqrt{5}$, and $BC =\sqrt{3^{2}+4^{2}}=5$,\\
$\because AB^{2}+AC^{2}=25$ and $BC^{2}=25$,\\
$\therefore AB^{2}+AC^{2}=BC^{2}$,\\
$\therefore \angle BAC=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore S_{\triangle ABC} =\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot AB=\frac{1}{2}BC\cdot AD$,\\
$\therefore \sqrt{5}\times 2\sqrt{5}=5\times AD$,\\
$\therefore AD=\boxed{2}$,
